4.4 CONSUMPTION EXPENDITURE
The average monthly consumption expenditure per 
household was Tk. 30,603 in 2022 at the national 
level. The average consumption expenditure in rural 
areas was Tk. 26,207 per month, whereas, in urban 
areas, it was Tk. 39,971. In 2016, it was Tk. 15,420, Tk. 
13,868 and Tk. 19,383 in the national, rural and urban 
areas, respectively. The monthly average consumption 
expenditure in 2022 increased by 98.46% in 2016 and 
413.13% in 2005.
Table 4.4 gives the estimates for monthly expenditure 
and consumption expenditure per household. At the 
national level, the average monthly expenditure per 
household was estimated at Tk. 31,500 at the current 
price in 2022. It was Tk. 26,842 in rural areas and Tk. 
41,424 in urban areas. The average monthly expenditure 
shows an increasing trend. At the national level, it was 
Tk. 15,715, Tk. 11,200 and Tk. 6,134 in HIES 2016, 2010 
and 2005 respectively.

The table includes key water quality indicators: pH, TDS, Cl, SO4, Na, K, Ca, Mg, Total Hardness, and WQI. These parameters are essential indicators used to assess the quality of water. # Data set

Published: 12 September 2024| Version 1 | DOI: 10.17632/trpd3rb29f.1

Contributor:

Priskilla James

## Description

The data contains measurements of the water quality from different monitoring stations, together with information about the locations, states, and station codes. Temperature, dissolved oxygen (D.O. ), pH, and conductivity are important metrics that are assessed because they represent fundamental water properties. In order to indicate the presence of organic matter and possible contamination, it also includes biochemical oxygen demand (B.O.D. ), nitrate and nitrite levels, and bacterial counts for total and fecal coliforms. The dataset, which includes average values and the year of collection, aids in the assessment of water quality over time.

# Replication Materials for “Did Safer Drinking-Water Sources Deliver Safer Water to Drink? Paired Source and Household Evidence from Three National Surveys in Bangladesh, 2012–2025”

Published: 30 September 2026| Version 1 | DOI: 10.17632/55syh9tkj9.1

Contributor:

Md. Mominul Islam

## Description

This repository contains replication materials for the manuscript “Did Safer Drinking-Water Sources Deliver Safer Water to Drink? Paired Source and Household Evidence from Three National Surveys in Bangladesh, 2012–2025.” The study examines whether drinking-water sources that test microbiologically safe also deliver safe water at the household or point of use, using nationally representative Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) water-quality data from 2012–13, 2019, and 2025. The three survey rounds are analysed as independent repeated cross-sections. The harmonized paired analytical sample contains 14,298 households with valid microbiological measurements at both the tested drinking-water source and the household/point of use: 2,302 observations from 2012–13, 6,052 from 2019, and 5,944 from 2025. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Hydrochemistry and weathering processes in the lower Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna River system, Bangladesh: Implications for CO2 sequestration and fluxes to the ocean

Published: 15 January 2025| Version 1 | DOI: 10.17632/8pksht5ptf.1

Contributor:

Md. Jaker Hossain

## Description

In this investigation, we examine the major ion compositions for the rivers of lower GBM Basin (Na+, K+, Ca2+, Mg2+, F-, Cl-, SO42-, HCO3-), using original data from December 2019 to January 2020. The high density of sampling and historical data was extensively analyzed, allowing us to (1) show spatial, daily, and vertical variations and long-term trends in major ions, (2) investigate the processes governing the major element chemistry in the basin, (3) evaluate seaward solute fluxes and source apportionment, and (4) estimate the weathering and CO2 sequestration rate in the study site.
